title: OpenCheckoutMandate
description: An open Checkout Mandate: signed by the user, carrying the limits within which an agent may later assemble and purchase a checkout. Not yet bound to any transaction, which is exactly why it must be bound to an agent — agent_key is what stops a stolen open mandate being usable by a different agent. Open mandates are not the obsolete v0.1 'Intent Mandate'; they are a different mechanism, and a verifier is always handed a closed mandate, never this.
$comment: agent_key is the public key of the agent this mandate authorises: a closed mandate signed by any other key must be rejected. AP2 carries it as the RFC 7800 'cnf' claim; that claim name is an encoding detail and lives in the adapter.

constraints.description: The limits the user approved. Evaluated by the verifier against the closed mandate the agent presents.

issued_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp at which this mandate was issued.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp after which this mandate must not be accepted. Should be the smallest value that lets the agent finish the task it was given — an open mandate is a standing authorisation, so its lifetime is its blast radius.
